title: 相量形式的 KCL：有效值不能直接相加
statement: 两个同频电流源 i_s1(t) = 3√2 cos(1000t) A，i_s2(t) = −4√2 sin(1000t) A 一起向结点 a 注入电流，经理想电流表 A 流入电阻 R = 10 Ω。
求电流表读数（有效值）、电阻电流 i_R 的初相和结点电压 u_a 的有效值。

questions.ask: 电流表 A 的读数 = ?

choices: 电流表有内阻，读数偏小
KCL 对瞬时值和相量成立，对有效值一般不成立；两电流相差 90°，要按相量相加
正弦电路中 KCL 不成立
i_s2 前面有负号，应为 4 − 3 = 1 A
choiceExplain: 题中电流表是理想的；而且它串在电流源驱动的支路里，内阻也不会改变电流。差别来自相位，不是仪表。
KCL 在正弦电路中对瞬时值和相量都成立；不成立的只是“有效值直接相加”。
负号只让相位改变 180°；4 − 3 = 1 A 要求两电流正好反相，而这里 −sin 化为 cos 后两者相差 90°。
questions.explain: Σi = 0 对每一瞬间成立，所以对相量成立：İ = İ_s1 + İ_s2。有效值只是模，两电流相位不同时 |İ_s1 + İ_s2| ≠ I_s1 + I_s2；这里相差 90°，I = √(3² + 4²) = 5 A。

hints: 先把两个电流都化成 cos 形式的有效值相量：−sin x = cos(x + 90°)。
对结点 a 用相量形式的 KCL：İ_R = İ_s1 + İ_s2，再化成极坐标形式。

en.title: KCL in phasor form: rms values don't simply add
statement: Two current sources of the same frequency, i_s1(t) = 3√2 cos(1000t) A and i_s2(t) = −4√2 sin(1000t) A, both inject current into node a; it flows through the ideal ammeter A into the resistor R = 10 Ω.
Find the ammeter reading (rms), the initial phase of the resistor current i_R and the rms value of the node voltage u_a.

questions.explain: I_s1 = 3∠0° A, I_s2 = 4∠90° A; KCL: I_R = I_s1 + I_s2 = 3 + j4 = 5∠53.13° A, and the ammeter reads the rms value 5 A.
I_R = 3 + j4 has angle arctan(4/3) = 53.13°, so i_R = 5√2 cos(1000t + 53.13°) A.

questions.ask: Why is the reading not 3 + 4 = 7 A?
choices: The ammeter has internal resistance, so it reads low
KCL holds for instantaneous values and phasors, not in general for rms values; the two currents are 90° apart and must be added as phasors
KCL does not hold in sinusoidal circuits
i_s2 has a minus sign, so it should be 4 − 3 = 1 A
choiceExplain: The ammeter is ideal, and since it is in a branch driven by current sources its resistance would not change the current anyway; the difference comes from phase, not the meter.
KCL holds in sinusoidal circuits for instantaneous values and for phasors; what fails is adding rms values directly.
A minus sign only shifts the phase by 180°; 4 − 3 = 1 A would need the currents in exact antiphase, but after converting −sin to cos they are 90° apart.
questions.explain: Σi = 0 holds at every instant, hence for phasors: I = I_s1 + I_s2. An rms value is only a magnitude, and when the phases differ |I_s1 + I_s2| ≠ I_s1 + I_s2; here they are 90° apart, so I = √(3² + 4²) = 5 A.

hints: Write both currents as cosine-based rms phasors first: −sin x = cos(x + 90°).
Apply phasor KCL at node a: I_R = I_s1 + I_s2, then convert to polar form.
solution: **2. Phasor KCL.** I_R = I_s1 + I_s2 = 3 + j4 = **5∠53.13° A**. The ammeter reads **5 A**, ψ = **53.13°**.
**3. Resistor voltage.** U_a = R·I_R = **50∠53.13° V**, rms 50 V.
